title: Posterior filtering, prior rollout, and KL-routing audit
purpose: Keep posterior filtering, posterior-anchored one-step prior, and no-reset open-loop errors separate; verify their observation visibility; and freeze the forward arithmetic and scope labels of a Dreamer-style KL-routing diagnostic.
allowed_claims: The fixed seeded fixture has higher prior-only open-loop RMSE than observation-corrected filtering RMSE.
The fixed posterior-anchored one-step prior RMSE lies between filtering and no-reset open-loop RMSE, but this ordering is fixture-specific.
Adding one authored unit to every observation after initialization changes filtering and posterior-anchored one-step metrics while leaving true open-loop metrics exactly unchanged.
Filtering, open-loop, and persistence measurements use the same generated trajectory.
The two authored KL cases place raw KL on opposite sides of a one-nat free-nats threshold.
Dynamics and representation branches share the same forward KL value while retaining different declared gradient targets; no gradient is measured.
forbidden_claims: The fixture is a trained neural RSSM or reproduces PlaNet or Dreamer.
The fixture estimates population performance, training convergence, GPU use, planning utility, or deployment safety.
Low filtering error proves that prior-only imagined rollouts are accurate.
A posterior-anchored one-step prior metric is an open-loop or H-step rollout metric.
The authored observation offset estimates real posterior leakage prevalence or model robustness.
The standard-library KL fixture verifies automatic differentiation, encoder or prior gradients, optimization, posterior collapse, or Dreamer training.
The locked DreamerV3 free-nats value and loss scales are universal RSSM defaults.

systems.name: categorical_kl_route_audit
systems.type: standard-library exact categorical KL and threshold arithmetic
outputs: clamped dynamics and representation forward values
systems.preprocessing: validate finite positive equal-length probability vectors that sum to one; compute KL(posterior || prior), then clamp each forward branch at one nat

datasets.name: procedural 1D partially observed trajectory
datasets.split_definition: One 32-state trajectory generated once with seed 7; the same 31 transitions are used for all compared branches.
leakage_controls: No parameters are fitted to the generated trajectory.
Filtering, open-loop, and persistence use identical actions and ground-truth positions.
Future observations are unavailable to the open-loop branch.
The future-observation offset negative control must leave the open-loop branch bit-for-bit unchanged while altering observation-consuming branches.

datasets.name: procedural two-case categorical KL threshold table
datasets.split_definition: Posterior is fixed at (0.5,0.5); small prior is (0.55,0.45), large prior is (0.99,0.01); free_nats=1.0 and dynamics/representation scales are 1.0/0.1.
leakage_controls: Both categorical pairs, threshold, scales, and KL direction are fixed before evaluation.
Raw KL is retained separately from the thresholded loss.
Stop-gradient targets are reported only as contract labels because the fixture has no automatic differentiation graph.
Values from the locked DreamerV3 commit are not generalized to other RSSM implementations.

protocol.comparison_unit: four paired prediction views on the same 31 transitions, one authored future-observation visibility perturbation, and two categorical posterior-prior cases

randomness.rationale: Trajectory process and observation noise are stochastic, but the authored smoke freezes seed 7; both KL cases are deterministic authored inputs. One trajectory seed does not estimate seed variability.

protocol.action_space: scalar deterministic sinusoidal action schedule with an authored periodic offset
protocol.timing: one abstract transition per step; no wall-clock or controller-frequency claim
termination_conditions: Generate exactly 32 states and evaluate the following 31 transitions.
Evaluate each of the two frozen categorical posterior-prior cases exactly once.
protocol.comparison_design: Compute posterior filtering, posterior-anchored one-step prior, no-reset open-loop, and persistence errors against the same latent positions without dropping steps; report open-loop absolute error at registered horizons. Then offset only observations after initialization and require the open-loop metric to remain exactly invariant while observation-consuming branches change. Separately compute raw and one-nat-clamped KL for both authored probability pairs.
protocol.selection_protocol: Observation and velocity gains, seed, step count, probability pairs, KL direction, threshold, and branch scales are fixed before evaluation; no result-dependent selection is allowed.
protocol.failure_definition: A run is invalid if it emits a non-finite metric, uses a transition count other than 31, resets the open-loop state from a posterior, lets the future-observation perturbation change open-loop output, omits a registered horizon or KL case, changes the KL direction/threshold/scales, or accepts an invalid trajectory/probability vector.

metrics.name: filtering_rmse
metrics.aggregation: root mean squared filtered-position error over all 31 transitions

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: A single frozen seed is a regression fixture, not a repeated-seed estimate.

metrics.name: open_loop_rmse
metrics.aggregation: root mean squared prior-only position error over all 31 transitions

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The fixed trajectory supports exact regression comparison only; it does not support a population interval.

metrics.name: persistence_rmse
metrics.aggregation: root mean squared previous-observation error over all 31 transitions

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The baseline is evaluated on one frozen regression fixture rather than sampled deployments.

metrics.name: categorical_raw_kl
metrics.split: reported separately for the small and large authored posterior-prior mismatches
metrics.aggregation: sum posterior_i * log(posterior_i / prior_i) over both categorical entries

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Both values are deterministic arithmetic on authored categorical vectors, not population estimates.

metrics.name: free_nats_clamped_forward_kl
metrics.split: small versus large mismatch and dynamics versus representation branch
metrics.aggregation: apply max(raw_KL, 1.0) separately to both forward branches; branches share a value but retain distinct declared gradient targets

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The fixture has no automatic differentiation graph. Equal forward values and target labels are deterministic contract evidence only.

metrics.name: scaled_total_kl_loss
metrics.aggregation: 1.0 * dynamics_loss + 0.1 * representation_loss after each branch is clamped at one nat

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The scales mirror one locked DreamerV3 configuration for an arithmetic fixture and are not estimated hyperparameters or universal defaults.

metrics.name: posterior_anchored_one_step_prior_rmse
metrics.aggregation: root mean squared one-step prior error over 31 transitions, with each prior initialized from the previous observation-corrected posterior

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: This is a deterministic visibility diagnostic on one frozen trajectory, not an open-loop population estimate.

metrics.name: open_loop_absolute_error_by_horizon
metrics.aggregation: absolute error on the single no-reset prior rollout at horizons 1, 4, 8, 16, and 31

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Five points on one rollout expose horizon identity but do not establish monotonic error growth or a confidence interval.

metrics.name: future_observation_visibility_audit
metrics.aggregation: compare full-trajectory RMSE before and after offsetting observations 1 through 31 while preserving actions, truth, and the initial observation

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The offset is an authored structural probe; it is not sampled corruption or robustness evidence.

distribution_shift.rationale: No train/calibration/test population or uncertainty estimator exists in this data-flow smoke.

disaggregations: posterior filtering versus posterior-anchored one-step prior versus no-reset open loop
dynamics-prior versus representation-posterior declared gradient target
reporting.raw_predictions: Recompute trajectory errors and both complete categorical pairs from the source; no large prediction artifact is emitted.
reporting.failure_artifacts: Invalid shape, action-conditioning, posterior-correction, and rollout-gap behavior is covered by chapter unit tests.
confounders: One authored dynamics process and one seed are used.
The model gains are hand-set rather than learned.
Filtering has observation access that prior-only rollout deliberately lacks.
The posterior-anchored one-step prior repeatedly starts from an observation-corrected state and therefore is not an H-step open loop.
The +1 observation offset is deliberately artificial and only audits branch visibility.
The KL cases use binary authored distributions rather than learned stochastic latents.
Gradient targets are source-derived labels and are not measured by automatic differentiation in this standard-library fixture.
reporting.missing_value_policy: All 31 transitions, both KL cases, four branch RMSE metrics, five registered open-loop horizons, the complete visibility negative control, and all three KL metric families are required; no imputation, truncation, reset, or failed-step/case filtering is allowed.

limitations: The model and trajectory are one-dimensional teaching constructions.
One seed cannot characterize stochastic variability or confidence intervals.
The two categorical KL cases cannot characterize training dynamics, posterior collapse, gradient magnitudes, or optimization stability.
The one-nat threshold and 1.0/0.1 scales describe the locked DreamerV3 snapshot used by the chapter and are not universal RSSM settings.
The benchmark does not measure closed-loop planning, neural training, GPU resources, or real-system validity.
